note: Every upstream BEMBEL reads, one entry per source. Liveness is checked by scripts/verify_sources.py; the shape is enforced by scripts/validate_data.py against data/schema/sources.schema.json. This registry is not shipped data — data/ATTRIBUTION.json remains the licence record for the datasets bundled into the app.

tiers.1: keyless, live, load-bearing. Ship without these and the app is empty.
tiers.2: keyless, live, high value, not load-bearing.
tiers.3: requires registration, key or certificate. Onboarding cost.
tiers.4: static or slow-moving reference data. Vendored at build time.
tiers.5: no API exists. Candidate for an agent-operator pipeline.

field_notes.cadence: How often BEMBEL should poll, not how often upstream changes.
field_notes.verified_at: Date a live request confirmed this entry. Re-run the verifier past ~90 days.
field_notes.searched_at: Tier 5 only: date the search for an API came up empty.
field_notes.observed: Values read at verification. The verifier compares live readings against these and reports drift.
field_notes.license: dl-de/by-2-0 = Datenlizenz Deutschland Namensnennung 2.0, attribution required.
field_notes.tier: Tier 1-2 failures are actionable and alert; tier 4 is vendored at build time and is only reported.

sources.name: DWD Wetterbeobachtungen (POI)
sources.station: 10637 = Frankfurt/Main (EDDF). The only reporting POI station inside the city; 10635 is Kleiner Feldberg at 805 m and 10641 is Offenbach-Wetterpark. Names come from the MOSMIX station catalogue, whose LAT/LON columns are degrees.decimal-minutes, not decimal degrees.
gotchas: Three header lines, not one: parameter names, units, then German labels. Read the column by name from line 1 and the unit from line 2 — index and unit are both assumptions that will eventually be wrong.
German decimal comma. '---' means the station did not report that hour; it is not zero, and several columns in this file legitimately are zero.
Timestamps are UTC and two-digit-year ('23.08.26;18:00'). Foundation's default two-digit window starts in 1950, so an unpinned parser reads 26 as 1926.
Rows arrive newest-first; nothing documents that, so sort rather than index [0].
sources.note: Chosen over brightsky for BEM-G06: this is DWD's own file, which keeps a hosted third-party service out of the critical path (ADR 0008). The thermometer stands on the airfield and reads cooler than the Innenstadt on hot afternoons — the app names the station for exactly that reason.

sources.name: DWD RADOLAN RV (Regen-Nowcast)
gotchas: The nowcast composites in this directory are HDF5 (`composite_rv_*.tar` holds `-hd5` files). The parseable classic RADOLAN binary is `DE1200_RV<stamp>.tar.bz2` / `DE1200_RV_LATEST.tar.bz2` in the same directory.
bzip2 is absent from Apple's Compression framework, but libbz2.tbd ships in every Apple SDK — a system library, not a dependency.
No-data is 0x29C4 and the 0x2000 flag bit; both must stay nil, never 0 mm.
Read the header: GP is rows x columns, PR is the scale exponent, VV the forecast step. Nothing is safe to hardcode.
sources.note: One tar archive covers the whole two-hour forecast. This is an observation-free product: it starts at the measurement and runs forward, which is why the past comes from dwd_radolan_ry instead.

sources.name: DWD RADOLAN RY (Regen-Beobachtung)
sources.grid: Classic RADOLAN 900×900 at 1 km, SW corner 46.9526/3.5889 — NOT DE1200. Frankfurt = row 346, column 424.
gotchas: Different grid from RV. Reading RY with DE1200's corner returns an in-bounds cell about 150 km north — silently wrong, never throws. Check the header's GP field.
The header writes the geometry as `GP 900x 900`, with spaces inside the field.
No VV field: it is an observation, so the forecast step is absent rather than 0.
The URL checked here is the directory. Individual filenames carry a UTC timestamp (raa01-ry_10000-YYMMDDhhmm-dwd---bin.bz2) and 404 once they roll off.
A composite is not on the server the instant its timestamp says — back off one five-minute step.
sources.note: One file per frame, so an hour of past is twelve requests against a public service every five minutes per user. BEM-F03 caps it at one hour for that reason; two hours would double it for a question the last hour already answers.

sources.name: DWD Wetterwarnungen
gotchas: Wrapped in warnWetter.loadWarnings({...}); — strip the callback before JSON.parse.
Keyed by Warncell-ID. 106412000 = Frankfurt, 106434000 = Hochtaunuskreis.
sources.note: Not read by the app: NINA's dashboard already relays DWD's warnings as provider 'DWD', so BEM-G03 needs no JSONP client. Kept for the Warncell-keyed detail the NINA relay drops.

sources.name: Bright Sky (DWD wrapper)
sources.note: clean JSON over DWD MOSMIX/observations. No key, no rate limit published. Not read by the app: BEM-G06 checked DWD's own POI files first and they parse directly (dwd_poi), so the hosted wrapper stays out of the critical path per ADR 0008. Kept as the documented fallback if opendata.dwd.de ever stops publishing POI.

sources.name: NINA / MoWaS Bevölkerungswarnungen
gotchas: The region key is the 12-digit Regionalschlüssel, not the 8-digit AGS. dashboard/06412000.json is HTTP 400; dashboard/064120000000.json is 200.
ARS is not AGS with zeros appended — below Kreis level the two lay their digits out differently, so 150853700000 for Wernigerode is not a key at all.
Only the Kreis form is derivable from an AGS: first five digits plus seven zeros. That is what BEMBELKit queries — 1/9/26 requests for the three rings.
Filter client-side by geocode if you use the mapData feeds; they are nationwide.
A DWD warning appears as dwd.… in the dashboard and dwdmap.… in dwd/mapData.json. Fetch the detail by the dashboard row's own id.
CAP ships a DE-LS block: that is Leichte Sprache, not the German text. Match language 'de'/'de-DE' exactly.

MOWAS tags German 'de', DWD tags it 'de-DE'. DWD writes
into instruction; MOWAS does not.
sources.note: dashboard/<ars>.json is BBK's own region filter and aggregates MOWAS, KATWARN, BIWAPP, LHP and DWD. The nationwide mapData feeds carry no geocode at all, so filtering those to a region would mean point-in-polygon over every warning in Germany. The card text comes from warnings/<id>.json.

sources.name: Umweltbundesamt Luftdaten API v3
sources.note: HLNUG has no machine-readable endpoint of its own; UBA republishes the Länder networks, and its 'Hessen' network IS the HLNUG Luftmessnetz. 35 Hessen stations, 4 inside Frankfurt (636 Ost and 763 Schwanheim are Hintergrund, 669 Friedberger Landstraße is Verkehr).
gotchas: The documented host is a redirect: umweltbundesamt.de/api/air_data/v3 answers 301 to luftdaten.umweltbundesamt.de/api/air-data/v3 — new host, underscore became a hyphen.
airquality/json WITHOUT a station parameter does not answer at all: 40s, zero bytes. Always name a station.
network=... on stations/json is silently ignored — asking for Hessen returns all 405 active stations (92 KB).
Three endpoints, three envelopes: components has rows at the top level, stations has data{key:row}, airquality has data{station:{hour:row}}.
data_incomplete=1 means 'not every component the index wants is present', not bad data. Every Verkehr station trips it — they measure no ozone.
The per-component 'y' is the position INSIDE its band, so 38 ug/m3 ozone and 121 both read ~0.65. Fold the band index back in before drawing a bar.
Cells change type between endpoints: station latitude is a quoted string, component values are bare numbers.

gotchas: Citizen sensors. exact_location=0 means the coordinate is fuzzed. Don't present as precise.
Mixed sensor types (SDS011, BMP180, DHT22) — filter by value_type before averaging.
sources.note: Citizen sensors, not a reference network. The authoritative air-quality reading comes from uba_luftdaten (BEM-G02); this stays the Hitzeinsel/temperature angle.

sources.name: Drive-time / live-traffic routing
sources.finding: There is no free live-traffic drive-time API for Germany. TomTom Routing (free tier ~2500 req/day) or HERE are the realistic choices. Autobahn warnings give incident context but not an ETA.
sources.note: Fallback: Openrouteservice / Valhalla give free routing WITHOUT live traffic — acceptable for "Fahrzeit zum Flughafen bei freier Strecke" plus an Autobahn-warning badge. Cheaper and arguably more honest than a fake ETA.
